title: Sampling: Types and Sample Design
summary: Population vs sample; probability sampling (simple random, stratified, cluster, systematic); non-probability (convenience, purposive); characteristics of good sample design; sampling with/without replacement.
objectives: List probability and non-probability sampling methods.
Describe characteristics of good sample design.
revision: Population = whole group; sample = subset. Probability: simple random, stratified, cluster, systematic. Non-probability: convenience, purposive.
traps: Simple random = equal chance for every member.
Stratified sampling ensures representation of subgroups.
confusions: Believing convenience sampling is probability sampling.

notes.t: The entire group about which the researcher wants to draw conclusions.
A subset of the population selected for the actual study.

r: Every member has an equal chance of selection.
Population divided into strata; random sample from each.
Population divided into clusters; entire clusters randomly selected.
Every nth member selected from a list.

i: Purposive (judgmental) sampling — researcher selects based on purpose.
Appropriate size for the research question.

notes.t: Simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic are probability methods; convenience and purposive are non-probability. UGC NET often asks to classify a method.

mnemonics.title: SSCS CNP
mnemonics.text: Probability: Simple random, Stratified, Cluster, Systematic. Non-probability: Convenience, Purposive.
